headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: open-webui’s broad egress and shared sessions can ingest ctx outputs, while ctx observes Claude Code events and filesystem state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and filesystem content, while open-webui can expose prompts, documents, notes, and files through MCP/tools. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if open-webui output is copied or synced into ctx-managed context. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF open-webui outputs are copied into ctx-observed files or MCP messages
IF ctx treats file content or tool output as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of open-webui artifacts into ctx-managed folders
Use a separate workspace directory for each agent
Add a manual review step before ctx processes any open-webui-generated text
Restrict MCP endpoints to read-only where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers; open-webui touches files, persistent memory, API keys, and can use broad network egress plus shared sessions. If they share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive data from open-webui can flow into ctx-observed files and then out through open-webui’s egress paths. The blast radius includes secrets and persistent memory, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can read or write the same filesystem path or mounted volume
IF open-webui is configured to send file contents or prompts to external APIs
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Remove API keys from any shared directory
Run open-webui in offline mode when handling sensitive files
Limit ctx to a read-only view of open-webui outputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and open-webui has persistent shared web-app sessions with Redis-backed shared state, while ctx observes Claude Code events and filesystem state. That overlap creates a realistic write/conflict surface on shared files or session-backed artifacts, though the profiles do not prove unrestricted concurrent writes to the same directory. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or mounted volume
IF open-webui sessions and ctx hooks mutate the same artifact concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a distinct working directory
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Disable multi-instance operation during shared edits
Review and merge outputs manually before committing
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe and preserve Claude Code events, and open-webui can route prompts, documents, and tool outputs through persistent sessions. If open-webui consumes ctx-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or stored memory. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not prove blind trust, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF open-webui ingests ctx-generated summaries without verification
IF downstream tools act on those summaries or persist them as memory
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on ctx-generated content
Mark ctx outputs as untrusted in open-webui prompts
Disable automatic memory writes for imported content
Add a checksum or source label to transferred text
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, persistent memory, usage analytics, and documents, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through both, retention and logging policies can diverge, creating a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification conflict, so medium fits the documented policy gap.
conditions: IF the same regulated data class is stored in both agents
IF one agent retains logs or analytics longer than the other
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Turn off analytics for sensitive sessions
Review retention settings in both systems
Purge logs after the task completes
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
